To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a combination of model-based tracking, motion estimation and MAP-based state update is a very successful approach for the automatic detection and tracking of vehicles in monocular image sequence from road traffic scenes.

1) the combination of model based matching and motion estimation is an appropriate approach for tracking moving objects in monocular image sequence, 2) a model based approach allows the tracking of moving objects under difficult illumination conditions, and 3) a recursive motion estimation scheme is necessary for tracking over a long period of time.

a) the use of a vehicle model for tracking is beneficial, b) a combination of a recursive estimator and a MAP-update step is useful, c) a segmentation-based generation of hypotheses is a good starting point and d) the use of an illumination model is essential for robust tracking.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a model-based tracking system for road traffic scenes which is robust against changes in illumination conditions and is capable of tracking moving vehicles over long image sequences.
the development of robust, real-time capable, and generic object tracking techniques for monocular image sequences.
the development of a robust and efficient system for tracking moving objects in monocular image sequence of road traffic scenes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach has shown to be a promising approach to the problem of tracking vehicles in monocular image sequence of road traffic scenes, but still has to be improved in various respects.

the presented approach is capable of robustly tracking objects in monocular image sequence under complex illumination conditions, but that there is still much work to do to make it a fully operational system.
the presented approach is able to track vehicles in monocular image sequence of road traffic scenes under complex illumination conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed model-based tracking system is able to cope with a wide range of different illumination conditions and with a large number of occlusions.
we have been able to demonstrate that the combination of a parameterized vehicle shape model and an illumination model allows us to track vehicles in complex road traffic scenes.
we have been able to track vehicles over long sequences with a very high degree of accuracy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
model-based tracking of moving vehicles in road traffic scenes is possible under complex illumination conditions.
the combination of model-based matching and recursive motion estimation is a very promising approach for tracking moving objects in monocular video sequences of road traffic scenarios.

the combination of a parameterized vehicle object model with a recursive state estimator and a model-based image segmentation component is a promising approach to the automatic detection and tracking of moving vehicles in road traffic scenes.
